idiom_name: ES module namespace exporting a few functions (the module is the facade); class when it owns state
implementation_notes: The module is the facade: keep collaborator modules private, export only the handful of functions the application needs, and use the module boundary plus closures for hidden state. jQuery is the historical proof of concept ($.get and $.ajax are facades over XHR and the DOM), and modern code repeats the shape with export function convertVideo(...) over internal helpers. Use a class or object when the facade holds configuration or lifecycle, and keep export * out of the entry module so internals never become public by accident.
pitfalls: export * barrels silently re-export every internal name; export explicit names from the facade module.
Importing the facade and subsystem modules from the same consumer recreates the coupling and can produce cycles; discipline or lint rules must protect the boundary.
Module singletons and closures keep caches alive for the whole process; long-lived state needs explicit invalidation or it leaks across requests and tests.
